Now we need to find a linear diene that upon RCM will cyclize to give that cyclohexene. RCM of a diene forms a new internal double bond between the two terminal alkene carbons, releasing an alkene (often ethylene). The diene must have two terminal alkenes (or internal alkenes) such that after cyclization, the new double bond is formed between the two alkene carbons that were originally the terminal ends of the diene. The product double bond is the one formed by the metathesis. In the product, the double bond is at position 1 (i.e., between C1 and C2). So the new double bond formed by RCM must be the double bond between C1 and C2 of the cyclohexene. That means the two alkene carbons of the diene become C1 and C2 of the product. So the diene must have two terminal alkenes (or internal alkenes) that are at the ends of a chain that will become the ring after connecting them.

When two such alkenes react, you can get R-CH=CH-R (internal alkene) and CH2=CH2 (ethylene). So the new double bond is between the two R groups (the internal carbons). The terminal CH2 groups combine to form ethylene.
